'''Ron Milo''' ({{Langx|he|רון מילוא}}; born February 11, 1975) is a [[Professor]] of [[Systems Biology]] at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. He is Weizmann Dean of Education,<ref>[https://www.weizmann.ac.il/pages/about-institute/senior-scientific-officers Weizmann website]</ref> the chairperson of the Israel society of ecology and [[environmental sciences]]<ref>[https://www.isees.org.il The Israel Society of Ecology and Environmental Sciences]</ref> and the director of the Institute for environmental sustainability <ref>[https://www.weizmann.ac.il/sustainability/ Institute for environmental sustainability]</ref> at Weizmann. Formerly he was the chairperson of the Israel young academy.<ref>[https://young.academy.ac.il/?nodeId=808 Israel Young Academy website]</ref>

==Education==
Ron Milo was born in Haifa and educated in Kfar-Saba. At the age of 15 he won the National Physics Olympiad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE – RON MILO |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/plants/Milo/sites/plants.Milo/files/milo_ron_cv_w.pdf |access-date=2024-02-06}}</ref> He holds a bachelor's degree with honors in physics and mathematics<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ron Milo |url=https://molbio.princeton.edu/speakers/ron-milo |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=Department of Molecular Biology |language=en}}</ref> from the [[Hebrew University]] as part of the [[Talpiot program]], a master's degree in electrical engineering from Tel Aviv University<ref>{{Cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE – RON MILO |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/plants/Milo/sites/plants.Milo/files/milo_ron_cv_w.pdf |access-date=2024-02-06}}</ref> and a PhD in the laboratory of Professor [[Uri Alon]] at the Weizmann Institute of Science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=People |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/mcb/UriAlon/people |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=Uri Alon |language=en}}</ref> In 2006–2008, Milo was the first Harvard Systems Biology Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-02-09 |title=Community (2/9/07) {{!}} Harvard Medical School |url=https://hms.harvard.edu/news/community-2907 |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=hms.harvard.edu |language=en}}</ref> at [[Harvard Medical School]].

== Research ==
Milo harnesses the tools of quantitative thinking and [[systems biology]] to find solutions to the challenges of sustainability.<ref>[https://www.weizmann.ac.il/plants/Milo/home Milo lab]</ref> Milo’s goal is improving the ability of humanity to produce food more efficiently by creating new ways to fixate carbon dioxide from the air. His group  demonstrated for the first time an ability to convert carbon dioxide into sugar in a synthetically engineered E. coli.<ref> 
Gleizer, S., Ben-Nissan, R., Bar-On, Y. M., Antonovsky, N., Noor, E., Zohar, Y., ... & Milo, R. (2019).[https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(19)31230-9?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS0092867419312309%3Fshowall%3Dtrue Conversion of Escherichia coli to generate all biomass carbon from CO2]. Cell, 179(6), 1255-1263</ref><ref>Antonovsky, N., Gleizer, S., Noor, E., Zohar, Y., Herz, E., Barenholz, U., ... & Milo, R. (2016). [https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(16)30668-7?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS0092867416306687%3Fshowall%3Dtrue Sugar synthesis from CO2 in Escherichia coli]. Cell, 166(1), 115-125.</ref> 
 
Milo also leads a global accounting of biomass on earth giving a fresh perspective on the impact of humanity and the future of biodiversity.<ref>Elhacham, E., Ben-Uri, L., Grozovski, J., Bar-On, Y. M., & Milo, R. (2020). [https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-3010-5 Global human-made mass exceeds all living biomass]. Nature, 588(7838), 442-444.</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Laville |first=Sandra |date=2020-12-09 |title=Human-made materials now outweigh Earth's entire biomass – study |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2020/dec/09/human-made-materials-now-outweigh-earths-entire-biomass-study |access-date=2024-02-06 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> His work on the biomass distribution on Earth<ref>Bar-On, Y. M., Phillips, R., & Milo, R. (2018). [https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.1711842115 The biomass distribution on Earth]. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 115(25), 6506-6511.
</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Carrington |first=Damian |last2= |first2= |date=2018-05-21 |title=Humans just 0.01% of all life but have destroyed 83% of wild mammals – study |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2018/may/21/human-race-just-001-of-all-life-but-has-destroyed-over-80-of-wild-mammals-study |access-date=2024-02-06 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> is widely cited for example in BBC documentaries and served for an exhibition in the museum of Natural history in London. He also quantified the land, irrigation water use, and greenhouse gas emissions of dietary choices, and the needed changes required to minimize our impact on the planet.<ref>Eshel, G., Shepon, A., Makov, T., & Milo, R. (2014). [https://www.pnas.org/doi/abs/10.1073/pnas.1402183111?doi=10.1073%2Fpnas.1402183111 Land, irrigation water, greenhouse gas, and reactive nitrogen burdens of meat, eggs, and dairy production in the United States]. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 111(33), 11996-12001.</ref>
 
His book “Cell Biology by the Numbers”,<ref>[https://book.bionumbers.org/ Cell Biology by the Numbers]</ref> is freely available online and was translated to multiple languages. He is the founder of BioNumbers,<ref>[https://bionumbers.hms.harvard.edu/search.aspx BioNumbers]</ref> the database of useful biological numbers. His papers were cited over 50,000 times.<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=L-_d3akAAAAJ&hl=en Google Scholar]</ref>
